chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from his uncle Hamza ibn Bazie, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'O Ja'far, eat the quince, for it strengthens the heart and emboldens the timid.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of eating quince according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the Prophetic tradition of utilizing natural remedies for both physical and spiritual well-being, specifically linking the consumption of quince to cardiac strength and the fortification of courage. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the integration of bodily health with moral character, as seen in the advice given to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, a key figure in early Islamic history.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Baie, from his uncle Hamza Bin Bazie, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to Ja’far<sup>as</sup>: ‘Eat the Quince, for it strengthens the heart and emboldens the timid’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ from his uncle Hamzah ibn Bazi‘ who has said the following: “Abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
said to Ja‘far, ‘O Ja‘far, eat quince; it strengthens the heart and emboldens the coward heart.’”
